newsitem.title: USA: HORSE RACING- LUKAS EXTENDS STREAK WITH 50-1 SHOT.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING- LUKAS EXTENDS STREAK WITH 50-1 SHOT.

text.p: On Tuesday, when 3-year-old filly Sharp Cat was entered in Friday's Kentucky Oaks instead of the Kentucky Derby, it looked like D. Wayne Lukas would end his streak of saddling a horse in 16 straight Kentucky Derbies.
Lukas, trainer of the last two Derby winners (Thunder Gulch in 1995 and Grindstone last year) said Wednesday morning that Deeds Not Words, would march to the starting gate on Saturday.
The lightly-raced Alydar colt was 50-1 on the morning line, but Lukas believes the horse, despite his poor showing in the Grade 2 Lexington at Keeneland on April 20, can fare well.
"I was less than crazy about his race in the Lexington over at Keeneland," Lukas said.

"But then again we know that doesn't equal anything when you leave Keeneland, because we have history to show that. Swale (1984 Derby winner) ran last. Sea Hero ran sub par over there, and in my own case, Thunder Gulch ran a bad 4th in the Bluegrass. A lot of horses that ran well in Keeeneland -- Skip Away last year, Holy Bull -- there are a lot of examples.
"So, when you when you are a handicapper and look at theses things and see his last race is less than perfect you have to be careful with that."
Deeds Not Words, who has only won once in four career starts, is the most lightly raced of the 13 entrants but has worked well lately which was a major factor in the decision to race him.

"I really got to thinking about it earlier in the week, as he trained well, but the thing was his workout on Tuesday. We had worked him at six furlongs and change here, right before the Lexington, and we were all impressed, and then he went over there and didn't run as well as hoped." Lukas said.

"Then we come back and we work him again here and he looks very good again. After being here for 16 or 17 years, it has always been my contention that horses either have an affinity for this race track or they don't, and I may be dead wrong on this but I feel he does have it," Lukas added.
A strong performance by Deeds Not Words, who will be ridden by Corey Nakatani, will silence Lukas's critics who think he may have entered the horse only to keep his streak alive.
"We're rolling the dice a little bit, obviously," conceded Lukas, "we are not going to be favoured or do we plan to be favoured."

If that something is that he wins the Derby, it will be the third straight year Lukas will end up in the winner's circle on the first Saturday in May. And one thing is for sure, it will be the 17th straight year he'll be in the paddock before the "Run For The Roses."
